title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Locomotion 005 — Brake-Debt Support Cascade
principle: A braking contact can acquire support before it has canceled root velocity. Root momentum is repaid across successive support catches; first contact must not teleport the root to rest.

source.identity: Sonic the Hedgehog — Sonic the Hedgehog — Sega Genesis — asset 21628
source.whole_sheet_evidence: The entire 690x1558 PNG was visually inspected as one evidence corpus, including its labeled Basic Motion, Basic Motion (Angled), Full Speed, Full Speed (Angled), Skidding, Balance, Rolling / Jumping, Pushing, pipe/tunnel, hurt/death/continue, ending, and unused/prototype regions. The extraction uses only the general contrast between fast travel, braking/skid posture, and recovery/support organization; non-locomotion regions were context only.
source.rights_boundary: Copyright-restricted commercial-game sprite art used as study evidence only. No source pixels, palette, contours, costume, character proportions, sheet layout, frame arrangement, tracing, redistribution, or close imitation is embedded in this specimen. Every pose, rig mark, ground line, transition, and video frame is independently authored abstract ASCII.

OBSERVED: TSR identifies asset 21628 as Sonic the Hedgehog from the Sega Genesis game Sonic the Hedgehog and gives the sheet size as 690x1558 PNG.
Whole-sheet inspection shows distinct fast-travel/full-speed and skidding/braking families alongside ordinary/angled locomotion and recovery-context families.
The static sheet does not establish source-authentic exposure timing for decisive keys.
INFERRED: The brake-debt support cascade, all abstract pose geometry, root spacing, support ownership, contact confidence, weight transfer, anticipation, absorption, and recovery sequencing.
Every ONES/TWOS/FOURS timing assignment under STREET_FIGHTER/CAPCOM policy.
UNKNOWN: Source-authentic frame exposure, engine playback cadence, exact in-game root coordinates, exact source force distribution, and exact chronology between sheet cells.

timing_note: ONES/TWOS/FOURS are display-frame hold classes, never seconds. All decisive timings in this specimen are inferred because the static source sheet does not establish exposure timing.

keys.name: FAST_CARRY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root enters with established forward velocity; no braking claim yet.

keys.name: COUNTERLEAN_PREP
keys.causal_role: anticipation / braking posture before new support
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Counterlean begins while root keeps traveling; anticipation does not erase velocity.

keys.name: BRAKE_CATCH_A
keys.motion_arc_root_note: First braking foot earns support, but root still carries substantial forward velocity.

keys.name: ROOT_OVERRUN_A
keys.causal_role: momentum debt made visible after support acquisition
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root advances beyond first catch while support stays trusted; this is the anti-teleport key.

keys.name: BRAKE_CATCH_B
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Second catch takes ownership after the first support has reduced but not canceled root travel.

keys.name: DUAL_SUPPORT_ABSORB
keys.causal_role: absorption / widen base / dissipate remaining travel
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Dual support broadens the braking base; forward spacing shrinks but remains nonzero.

keys.name: SETTLE_RECOVERY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root spacing compresses to a small final drift while posture rises toward neutral.

keys.name: RESTACK
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root comes to rest only after the cascade of braking catches; both supports are trustworthy.
